simulator_description: The simulator models daily hospital bed occupancy and an explicit roster of in-hospital patients across three diseases by evolving an initial patient list forward in time with stochastic admissions and discharges. Each day, existing patients’ remaining length-of-stay is decremented and those who complete LOS are removed, while new arrivals for each disease are drawn from a time-varying, overdispersed (Gamma–Poisson/negative-binomial) arrival process scaled deterministically by the initial state to reflect cross-trajectory demand differences; each admitted patient is assigned ICU vs Standard via disease-specific probabilities and an LOS drawn from empirically learned discrete distributions (tilted to match target means) or a geometric fallback. Occupancy is computed directly from the roster (with an optional capacity-rejection rule), which makes the state internally consistent and aligns with hospital flow assumptions where arrivals drive census and LOS governs departures, while training-data ingestion of LOS and seasonal arrival profiles grounds the stochastic dynamics in observed patterns.
